about: Round 1 of the autonomous ending run (second-half-ending-goal.md). Kai has not noted this page yet. The plan lists every call Claude made in Kai's place, with its reason, 'Kai to rule' first. Full record: ../second-half-ending-log.md. Shown on the page by scripts/scene/build-timeline.py.

plan.h: Scene C: calls for you to rule on
items: KAI TO RULE: The lady's act in C01: she stops beside Maddie on the step, straightens the torn bunting and says "Go on, then. You lead." / Maddie: "Ooh. Ta." Why: lifting scene B's step ban at the moment it costs nothing would be a callback, not a turn, so she gives Maddie the lead instead. Must be checked against your vote scene when it exists.
KAI TO RULE: "Come in. Mind the step." (the AI at his own door, C07). Why: it pays off the lady's "You stay on the step" from scene B, spent once, and echoes beat 0's "Mind how you go".

KAI TO RULE: The seat row carries the cost: "Did you put the seat down?" / "We're not coming back, love." / "Did you put it down?" / "...Yes." Why: the film's most loved joke pays for the goodbye instead of a speech (every joke paired with an undeniable consequence). All words by: claude.

KAI TO RULE: C03 remade and cut from 22 s to 10.5 s: it opens at 160% on Maddie alone (rhyming beat 0's travelling shot), holds, then eases out so the hundred appear behind her. Why: the cold viewer's attention dropped in the 22 s walk. The 160% opening is soft (720p source).

KAI TO RULE: C06's visible cost: the old man stays on his feet, bent over his stick catching his breath, a hand on his back, the trolley of blankets tipped in the mud; the amber seam brightens end to end on the reveal. Why: a man lying down read as an event (cold viewer); tiredness and a dropped load is the cost without a new plot point.

KAI TO RULE: C05 opens at 140% on Derek, so Sandra's off-screen "Did you put it down?" has no shut mouth in frame, then eases back to the two of them on "...Yes.". Why: no footage of her saying it exists. The alternative is a re-shot C05; the 140% frame is soft.

KAI TO RULE: C07: in every take Maddie wanders left along the wall before going up the step. Kept t3 and laid "Come in. Mind the step." over its first 3 s so she enters on the invitation. Weak: it can read as hesitation.
KAI TO RULE: C02: a light breeze, the bunting hangs limp (C02-t4). Why: the strong-wind takes grew a pennant pole or streamed bunting across the frame.

KAI TO RULE: The building is the BL series (BL1-day for C06, BL4-seam-opens relit to day for C07). Why: they are the only stills that are the fixed design, a long low black-glass slab with one amber seam; L11 is a tall block and was dropped. Weak: at C07's distance the wall reads taller than BL1.

KAI TO RULE: Still picks: C01 r2-a (the only face big enough to lip-sync; flaw: the bunting is strung on a bar over the lid) and C07 r2-b (the seam parts into one doorway and step, Maddie small at its foot).

KAI TO RULE: Music: C-walk (lone violin and piano, Suno cc128cb2) enters on the long walk, mid-phrase under a 1.5 s fade, so its held low cello note lands on the building reveal with no edit inside the music; it ducks under the seat row and stops dead on "Mind the step". C01 and C02 play on wind, crowd and bunting only.
KAI TO RULE: Runtime 45.5 s, under the 60 to 90 s target. Why: cut to the real lines with the house LEAD/GAP/TAIL and no padding. Say if the walk needs more air.
KAI TO RULE: Look: scene B's overcast exterior, not full 1980s 16mm. Why: seamless continuity out of B's door; the second half travels from 16mm toward the futuristic.

plan.h: Scene C: other calls made in your place
items: The scene's sentence: trust you can check becomes trust you give, and giving it costs everything. Why: story-craft Build step 1, written as a hypothesis for the review to attack.
The vote is yours, so C opens straight on the walk out and assumes all hundred said yes, with no refuser. Why: the goal.
C03 is the scene's one moving camera; every other shot is camera-locked with pushes in post (C01 to 106%, C06 to 112%). Why: the hybrid method, and one moving shot that rhymes with beat 0.
The AI speaks through Maddie's speaker (small-speaker filter, beacon blips). Why: the 16 Oct ruling that the AI never gets a body.
Maddie's reference is clips/simulation/stills/s3/s3-bot-00b-a.jpg (the brief's clips/second-half/simulation/ path does not exist; this is the file canon names). Torn bunting in every shot.

Still picks C02 r2-a (Maddie leads from the foreground), C03 f1-a (Maddie large in the left third, the hundred well behind), C04 r2-a / C05 r2-a (a matched reverse pair, Derek in the same green jumper), C06 r2-c (exactly the one building, past the cost in the foreground).

Clip picks C01-t1, C02-t4, C03f chain (two linked Omni clips), C04-t2, C05-t2, C06-t2, C07-t3. Rejected: C07-t1 (smoke from the doorway reads as fire), C04-t1 and C05-t1 (Omni spoke 1.5 to 2 times faster than the voice).
Lip-sync placed phrase by phrase on the tracked mouths, never slowed; every onset within 0.05 s after its mouth opens. The lady's "Go on, then." at x1.25 is the one to watch for squeeze.
Derek's "We're not coming back, love" lifted 2.5 dB and the music ducked to -13 dB under it. Why: a reviewer heard "We're not back home"; the take is clean, so no re-voice.
C07's glass reflection that read as a second robot is darkened with a soft power window.

Sound made up for C: feet on chalk, a doorway hum, a happy beep after "Ta", a bump and boop up the step; the crowd bed crossfades across C02/C03; a low murmur under C07. No birdsong: the library has none.
"Come in. ... Mind the step." gap tightened from Suno's 1.85 s to 0.9 s (no word touched); "Bloody hell." waits 1.5 s into the reveal.
AI lines: Suno take 7f567949 (w10), word-perfect; a faint low drone is high-passed. The other C takes could not be heard (their rows scrolled out of the list).
C02 is graded to match C03's head; C03 is regraded with a ramp. The remaining big colour steps are changes of place (the doorway into daylight, a cloud shadow on the crest).
delivery-qc's range FAIL is left: the picture is clamped to 16-235 before the encode and x264 ringing pushes a few grain pixels over, as on scene A. Mix -16 LUFS is this run's target, not -14.
Not done in C, on purpose: the AI's own-interest line and a vote slate. Why: the line belongs on the wafer in D ("It only sends one back. Me."), the slate on the reel.
